jobs.title: Estrategia y Ejecución de Google Ads para Venta de Servicios
jobs.description:
Busco un/a freelancer con experiencia en Google Ads de Búsqueda y campañas orientadas a la venta de servicios profesionales. Es importante aclarar que no hemos hecho campañas de pago previamente.

El proyecto es para Capital Digital, una marca de estrategia, posicionamiento y comunicación digital. El objetivo no es generar alcance, likes ni tráfico sin propósito: buscamos vender uno de nuestros servicios mediante una campaña bien estructurada y medible.

No buscamos simplemente activar anuncios o promocionar publicaciones. La idea es crear un embudo de captación comercial completo, dirigido a personas o empresas con una necesidad activa: búsqueda en Google, anuncio relevante, landing page específica, formulario o canal de contacto, seguimiento y medición de resultados. Estamos abiertos a escucharte en caso de que trabajes con otras herramientas de promoción, como PPC.

La primera fase se trabajará únicamente con Google Ads de Búsqueda. Por el momento no se contempla Meta Ads, campañas Display, pop-ups, compra de clics ni tráfico masivo de baja calidad.

El sitio web y CRM están alojados en GoHighLevel. Podemos construir internamente las landing pages, formularios, páginas de agradecimiento, automatizaciones y pipeline de seguimiento necesarios. Sin embargo, buscamos a alguien que pueda aportar criterio estratégico para definir qué embudo necesitamos y qué elementos deben estar listos antes de invertir en la campaña.

Qué necesitamos principalmente:

* Recomendar cuál de nuestros servicios sería más conveniente promover primero, considerando intención de búsqueda, viabilidad comercial y posibilidad de venta.

* Proponer una estrategia inicial de Google Ads Search enfocada en generar oportunidades reales de venta.

* Investigar y seleccionar búsquedas y palabras clave con intención comercial, incluyendo negativas para evitar clics irrelevantes.

* Recomendar el enfoque de los anuncios, la oferta, el llamado a la acción y la estructura necesaria de la landing page.

* Configurar o supervisar la medición de acciones relevantes: envío de formulario, solicitud de información, clic a WhatsApp, reserva de una reunión u otra conversión acordada.

* Configurar y optimizar un piloto inicial de campaña, con un presupuesto limitado y previamente aprobado.

* Entregar reportes comprensibles sobre inversión, consultas, conversiones, calidad de oportunidades y recomendaciones.

Forma de trabajo esperada:

* Antes de activar inversión, requerimos una fase breve de análisis, recomendación y propuesta de implementación.

* Buscamos un piloto inicial de aproximadamente 21 a 30 días, sujeto a la recomendación del profesional.

* Capital Digital conservará la propiedad de la cuenta de Google Ads, dominio, sitio web, GoHighLevel/CRM, landing pages, datos, conversiones y facturación.

* El acceso se otorgará por invitación y con los permisos necesarios para trabajar; no se compartirán contraseñas ni datos de tarjetas.

* El método de pago y el presupuesto de la campaña serán gestionados por Capital Digital. Los honorarios profesionales se acordarán por separado.

* No se deberá aumentar el presupuesto, activar campañas adicionales ni abrir otros canales sin aprobación previa.

Al postular, por favor indica:

* Qué incluye exactamente tu servicio: estrategia, configuración, investigación de keywords, anuncios, medición, optimización y reportes.

* Qué información necesitarías de nuestra parte para comenzar.

* Qué recomendarías que construyamos nosotros en GoHighLevel y qué parte podrías implementar o supervisar tú.

* Tu propuesta de trabajo para el piloto, plazo estimado y entregables.

* Tus honorarios y qué tareas, si las hubiera, se cotizan por separado.

* Un ejemplo breve de una experiencia comparable con servicios profesionales, sin revelar información confidencial.

Valoramos especialmente propuestas transparentes, con un alcance realista, criterios de medición claros y recomendaciones basadas en intención de búsqueda y calidad comercial, no promesas genéricas de clics o resultados garantizados.

jobs.title: M&A Prospect Research & Appointment Setting Specialist

We are looking for a proactive and resourceful M&A Researcher / Business Development Specialist to identify, qualify, and engage potential acquisition targets based on a defined Investment Profile.

The objective is straightforward: build a high-quality MQL pipeline of companies that meet our acquisition criteria and convert qualified prospects into scheduled discovery calls.

This role goes beyond basic research. The right candidate will be responsible for identifying relevant businesses, validating their fit against our investment requirements, initiating outreach, and securing conversations with owners, founders, or key decision-makers.

Primary Objectives
Build a targeted and qualified M&A prospect / MQL list based on the provided Investment Profile.
Identify and engage business owners and key decision-makers.
Schedule qualified M&A Discovery Calls with interested prospects.

Scope of Work
Research potential acquisition targets within the technology sector based on predefined investment criteria.
Validate each prospect against key qualification requirements before outreach.
Identify appropriate owners, founders, executives, or other relevant decisionmakers.
Conduct outbound outreach through phone, email, LinkedIn, and other appropriate channels.
Introduce the acquisition opportunity professionally and assess initial interest in exploring a potential transaction.
Schedule discovery calls with qualified and interested prospects.
Maintain accurate prospect information, outreach activity, conversation notes, sentiment, and next steps in the CRM.
Provide warm handoffs to the M&A team once a qualified prospect agrees to further discussions.
Successful Outcome

A successful engagement will produce a consistent pipeline of well-qualified acquisition prospects that closely match the Investment Profile and result in scheduled conversations with business owners or decision-makers who are genuinely open to discussing a potential transaction.

Deliverable: a clean, fully formatted Word file ready for submission plus a brief change log highlighting significant fixes. If you use specialized tools or stylesheets (Word styles, EndNote, Zotero, etc.), just note that in the log so I can maintain consistency on future edits.

I need it completed within 3 hours

jobs.title: Legal Guidance on Deed Theft
jobs.description:
I am dealing with a deed-theft situation in which title to my property was transferred without my knowledge or consent. I need clear, actionable advice grounded in real-estate dispute law so I can pursue compensation for my losses and ensure the fraudulent transfer is reported to the appropriate criminal authorities.  

Here is what I expect from your assistance:  
• A concise assessment of the facts and any documents I provide, pinpointing which statutes, case law, or common-law principles apply to deed theft in my jurisdiction.  
• A step-by-step strategy outlining the civil remedies available to recover damages—whether through quiet-title action, tort claims, or other suitable causes—and how to calculate those damages realistically.  
• Guidance on coordinating with law-enforcement or prosecutorial agencies to trigger a criminal investigation alongside the civil claim, including how best to package evidence so it meets their intake standards.  
• A short memo summarising key deadlines, filing fees, and procedural traps to avoid, so I can decide whether to proceed pro se or retain counsel locally.  

Please ground your advice in real-world practice, cite primary authorities where relevant, and flag any jurisdiction-specific nuances that could alter the recommended course. Deliver the written overview in an editable document and be available for one follow-up clarification after I have reviewed it.

Entrego el archivo .AI con cada parte del cuerpo en capas separadas; tú te encargas de importarlo, riggear donde sea necesario y animar la acción completa en Adobe Animate. Al final necesito el archivo .FLA editable y una exportación en .MOV o .MP4 para revisión.

jobs.title: Composite Case Laminate & FEA
jobs.description:
I have a small two-piece case—a lid and a lower body—that both present A and B cosmetic sides. The goal is to define an efficient composite laminate schedule and verify its structural integrity through finite-element analysis. Both visible faces must end up with a high-gloss finish, so ply orientations, edge treatments, and any core breaks need to respect that surface requirement.

Here’s how I see the work flowing: I have a lay-up in mind but need to look at various options for plies, core, etc.(materials, ply count, orientation, any core or local reinforcements) and back it up with an FEA simulation that demonstrates the case can handle abuse..I want to be able to take this thing out to a field and see exactly what it takes to destroy it. I also want to use graphene as an additive in the resin. I have a supplier that is already using his material in body armor with great success. 

Deliverables  
• Laminate stack-up drawing or table, ready for tooling  
• FEA model and report: boundary conditions, load cases, results, safety factors  

Native files from tools such as SolidWorks, CATIA, NX, ANSYS, Abaqus, or similar are fine—whatever you are most comfortable with as long as I can review geometry and results.

Once I sign off on the laminate and the analysis meets the agreed acceptance criteria (no critical areas below a safety factor of 1.5), we’re done. I’m ready to start as soon as you are.

jobs.title: Initiative: Sentinel Ledger — Real-Time FinTech Risk Intelligence & Anomaly Surveillance Platform (Backend Engineering)
jobs.description:
*Initiative: Sentinel Ledger — Real-Time FinTech Risk Intelligence & Anomaly Surveillance Platform (Backend Engineering)*

We are seeking a senior systems architect or technical team to design, build, containerize, and operate the production backend for a real-time anomaly detection and threat-scoring platform for financial transactions.

This is not a proof-of-concept or an experimental sandbox. The final deliverable must be a fully hardened, real-time, fault-tolerant system built to run in live enterprise environments.

*System Overview*
The backend framework must:
- Ingest and process high-velocity transaction data continuously and without lag
- Detect irregular behavior using trained machine learning models, not static or hardcoded heuristics
- Publish live threat-assessment metrics through fast, low-latency endpoints
- Meet demanding throughput, response-time, and scaling requirements

Placeholder code, hardcoded logic, synthetic mock data, or simulated streaming endpoints will be treated as an automatic project default.

*Compensation & Milestone Schedule — GBP 2,300 Fixed, Paid in Two Stages*

_Stage 1 — GBP 2,185_
Released when the contract begins. Covers cloud resources, environment setup, and the initial core pipeline build.
Note: this payment is not delivery, review, or approval of the work. It does not waive any technical spec, throughput standard, or runtime target, and it does not limit legal recourse or clawback rights if the contract is breached.

_Stage 2 — GBP 115 (Final Settlement)_
Released only once:
- Production go-live is complete, end to end
- All microservices are active and reachable
- Latency and throughput metrics have been verified
- Full handover has taken place: source repos, model weights/artifacts, cloud/infra credentials, technical/architecture docs

If exit criteria aren't met, final payment is forfeited.

*What Needs to Get Built*
Leave out any piece below and the whole delivery counts as failed.

_Data Intake_
- Distributed streaming, running on Kafka and Spark Streaming
- Handles serious payload volume without falling behind, in real time
- Schema checks, cleanup, and validation baked into the pipeline itself

_Feature Engineering_
- One central place where computed features live
- Real-time streaming and offline batch computation running side by side

_Detection & Scoring_
- Anomaly detection that mixes statistical boundaries with recurrent LSTM models
- A weighted service that blends multiple models into one threat score
- Model inference that returns results in well under a second
- Fixed rule filters, hardcoded thresholds, or canned static responses won't cut it here.

_Making Predictions Explainable_
- SHAP-based explainability (or something equivalent)
- A plain-language reason attached to every score the model produces

_API & Application Layer_
- Built on FastAPI, organized into clean modules
- OAuth2/JWT handles enterprise authentication
- Structured to run as standalone microservices
- Complete OpenAPI/Swagger docs for anyone consuming the API downstream

_Infrastructure & DevOps_
- Kubernetes running across multiple nodes
- CI/CD automated end to end for builds and releases
- Grafana and Prometheus covering telemetry, logging, and observability
- Canary or blue-green deploys for safe rollouts
- A script that only runs locally, a docker-compose setup with no real scaling path, or anything that can't handle production traffic gets disqualified.

_Testing & QA_
- Load and concurrency testing pushed to peak volume
- A formal readiness check signed off before anything goes live

*Mandatory Performance Benchmarks*
The architecture must meet or exceed every one of these:
- Ingestion Rate: ≥ 50,000 events/sec
- Pipeline Latency: ≤ 2.0 seconds
- Feature Lookup: ≤ 50 milliseconds
- Model Precision: ≥ 90% true-positive anomaly rate
- Inference Compute Time: ≤ 80 milliseconds
- API Round-Trip Response: ≤ 400 milliseconds

Missing a single benchmark constitutes non-delivery.

*Uptime & Reliability*
99.5% uptime, tracked monthly. Usual carve-outs apply — scheduled maintenance, third-party vendor outages, force majeure, or unauthorized changes.

*Support Coverage*
Hours: 09:00–18:00 GMT/BST
- Sev 1 (everything's down): triage within 4 hrs, patched within 24 hrs
- Sev 2 (major functionality broken): triage within 8 hrs, patched within 48 hrs
- Sev 3 (small issue): triage within 1 business day, resolved within 5

*When Is This Actually Done?*
Sign-off happens only when, all at once:
- It's live and running in a real cloud environment
- Every listed component is up and checked
- The models are giving real predictions, not sample output
- Latency and throughput hold up under actual load
- CI/CD and monitoring are working
- Architecture docs and runbooks delivered
- Credentials, repos, and model files fully handed over

Half-finished doesn't count as finished here.

*Security, Governance & Regulatory Compliance*
Must follow safeguards aligned with ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, and applicable PCI-DSS standards. All pipelines must comply with UK/EU GDPR. Anonymized, non-attributable data may be used only where legally permitted.

*Intellectual Property Rights*
Once the final milestone is released, all custom code, model weights, config scripts, and documentation transfer entirely to the Employer. jobs.title: Moodle + IOMAD multi-tenant training platform with Stripe usage billing
jobs.description:
We are an Australian training company building a multi-tenant e-learning platform on Moodle with IOMAD. All course content already exists — this is a configuration and integration project, not content production.

Each client organisation logs in as its own tenant and administers everything itself. We do not want to perform enrolment administration on their behalf.

Core functionality

Tenant provisioning — each client organisation is an isolated IOMAD company with its own branding and login URL
Delegated administration — a Company Manager can create users, create classes, allocate course seats and run reports, with no access to site administration and no visibility of any other tenant
Shared course library — courses held once centrally and made available to nominated tenants, with participants from different tenants invisible to one another
Class creation — a manager creates a dated class, adds participants by name and email (individually or by CSV), and the system creates or matches accounts, allocates seats with an expiry date tied to the class, and sends branded invitation emails
Progress and completion tracking, exportable completion reports, certificates
Usage billing — each enrolment written to a ledger on the participant's first course access, transmitted to Stripe as meter events, producing one monthly invoice per tenant in AUD with GST
Video served from Cloudflare Stream or Mux via signed URLs, not stored in moodledata
Transactional email via Postmark or SendGrid with SPF, DKIM and DMARC configured

Environment

Elestio managed IOMAD in an Australian region, with separate staging and production. All custom code delivered to our Git repository under GPLv3. Documentation and runbooks are required so we can operate the platform ourselves after handover.

Not in scope

Course content, practical assessment, marketing website, student management system integrations.

To bid

Describe an IOMAD project you have delivered and your role in it.
Answer this: in IOMAD, what happens when a learner needs to belong to two companies at once, and what does each company's manager see?

Bids that do not answer question 2 will not be considered. A full scope document will be sent to shortlisted bidders.

Please see the attached full scope of the project. 

Many thanks
Mo

jobs.title: Build ML Anomaly Detection Backend
jobs.description:
Sentinel Ledger: Real-Time Risk & Anomaly Intelligence Backend

THE ROLE

We're hiring a senior backend architect (or a small team, if bidding as an agency) to build a production-grade, real-time transaction-monitoring system from the ground up. This isn't a prototype or a portfolio piece — the end result needs to run live, under real load, in a real enterprise environment, with real money moving through it.

Transactions flow in continuously, get scored for risk in near-real-time by trained ML models, and surface actionable alerts through a fast, well-documented API — all while the whole stack stays observable, scalable, and secure.

We won't accept stubbed-out logic, hardcoded thresholds standing in for real models, mocked data streams, or anything that only works in a demo. If it can't survive production traffic, it doesn't count.

WHAT YOU'LL BE BUILDING

1. Ingestion Layer
- A distributed streaming pipeline (Kafka + Spark Streaming) that keeps pace with high transaction volume in real time, with no backlog buildup
- Validation, cleanup, and schema enforcement built directly into the pipeline, not bolted on after

2. Feature Store
- A single, centralized feature repository
- Streaming and batch feature computation running in parallel, kept consistent with each other

3. Detection & Scoring Engine
- Hybrid anomaly detection: statistical thresholds combined with a trained LSTM (recurrent) model — no static rule sets pretending to be ML
- An ensemble layer that blends model outputs into a single weighted threat score
- Sub-second inference, every time

4. Explainability Layer
- SHAP (or a comparable method) attached to every prediction
- A human-readable explanation accompanying each score, no black-box outputs

5. API Layer
- FastAPI, cleanly modularized by domain
- OAuth2/JWT for enterprise-grade auth
- Each major function deployable as its own microservice
- Full OpenAPI/Swagger documentation

6. Infrastructure
- Kubernetes, multi-node, production-configured
- Full CI/CD, no manual build/deploy steps
- Observability via Prometheus + Grafana (metrics, logs, alerting)
- Canary or blue-green rollout strategy
- Local-only setups or docker-compose without a real scaling path will not pass review

7. QA & Load Validation
- Load and concurrency testing at peak projected volume
- A formal go/no-go readiness review before anything touches production

PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKS (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

- Ingestion throughput: 50,000+ events/sec
- End-to-end pipeline latency: 2.0 seconds or less
- Feature lookup time: 50 ms or less
- Model precision (true positives): 90% or higher
- Inference compute time: 80 ms or less
- API round-trip response: 400 ms or less

Missing any one of these means the deliverable isn't accepted.

Uptime target: 99.5%, measured monthly (standard exclusions apply: scheduled maintenance, third-party outages, force majeure, unauthorized changes).

POST-LAUNCH SUPPORT

Coverage window: 09:00 to 18:00 GMT/BST

Sev 1 (full outage): triage in 4 hours, resolved in 24 hours
Sev 2 (major feature broken): triage in 8 hours, resolved in 48 hours
Sev 3 (minor issue): triage in 1 business day, resolved in 5 business days

COMPENSATION

Total: £2,300 fixed, paid in two milestones

Milestone 1: £2,100, released at contract start to cover environment setup, cloud resources, and initial pipeline development. This payment does not constitute approval, sign-off, or a waiver of any technical requirement. All specs, benchmarks, and runtime targets in this brief remain fully in force regardless.

Milestone 2 (final settlement): £200, released only after full production go-live, all services verified active and meeting every latency/throughput benchmark, and complete handover (source code, model artifacts, credentials, and documentation). If exit criteria aren't met, this final payment is forfeited.

DEFINITION OF DONE

All of the following, simultaneously, no partial credit:
- Live in a real cloud environment, not a staging sandbox
- Every component listed above deployed and verified
- Models producing genuine predictions on real data
- Benchmarks holding under actual load, not synthetic tests
- CI/CD and monitoring fully operational
- Documentation and runbooks delivered
- All credentials, repositories, and model files transferred

Acceptance is binary. "Nearly done," "beta," and "mostly working" submissions are not accepted, and there's no prorated payment for partially completed modules.

COMPLIANCE & SECURITY

Must align with ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, and applicable PCI-DSS standards. All data handling must comply with UK/EU GDPR; synthetic or anonymized data may only be used where legally appropriate.

IP, CONFIDENTIALITY & LEGAL TERMS

IP transfer: Upon final payment, all custom code, models, configs, and documentation transfer fully to the Employer. The developer retains rights to any pre-existing generic tooling, boilerplate, or reusable infrastructure scripts not built specifically for this project.

Confidentiality: Indefinite, for both parties, covering architecture, workflows, models, live data, secrets, and configs.

Breach: Failure to deliver a fully functioning, benchmark-compliant production system is treated as material breach, entitling the Employer to terminate and seek recovery of funds paid.

Suspension rights: The developer may pause work for unpaid invoices (30+ days), Employer breach of core terms, discovered misuse, or an urgent unpatched security risk.

Liability: Standard statutory limits apply; no limitation on liability for death or injury from negligence, fraud, or non-waivable statutory duties.

Force majeure: Standard carve-outs for events outside either party's control.

Communication: All binding communication must occur through Freelancer.com; off-platform agreements carry no contractual weight.

Governing law: England and Wales, exclusive jurisdiction.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- A demonstrated track record deploying high-availability distributed systems to production, not just prototypes
- Deep hands-on experience with high-throughput streaming architectures
- Experience containerizing and operating ML systems at scale
- Strong working knowledge of Kafka, Spark, Kubernetes, and FastAPI

TO APPLY, INCLUDE

jobs.title: Real-Time 1xBet Crash Predictor

jobs.title: Reinstate Suspended Amazon Seller Account

I do not have any additional or second attempt to complete the verification. Submitted appeals multiple times but not getting proper response, just getting canned response. 

After reviewing the information from your virtual identity verification, we believe or our controls identified that your account has been used to engage in deceptive, fraudulent, or illegal activity. As a result, your account won't be reactivated.

Here is what I am looking for:  
• A clear action plan that outlines which documents must be resubmitted or amended and why they previously failed.  
• Hands-on help compiling those documents—passport or ID scans, utility bills, bank statements—so they meet Amazon’s formatting and authenticity guidelines.  
• Drafting an effective appeal letter (POA) that addresses Amazon Seller Performance in their preferred structure, tone, and level of detail.  
• Ongoing follow-up with Seller Support until the account is reinstated and selling privileges are fully restored.  

If you have a proven track record of successfully reinstating suspended accounts and know the exact wording, document standards, and timelines Amazon expects, I’d like to work with you right away.

jobs.title: Vintage CD Re-Issue Duplication
jobs.description:

I have only a high-quality digital copy of the record; you would start from that file, apply light sonic polishing—subtle EQ and level balancing rather than a full remaster—and then prepare everything for commercial replication.

The goal is 300–500 professionally pressed CDs. I want the discs, tray cards and booklet to look exactly the way they did in 2006, so please keep the cover art and liner notes intact. If you need to rebuild print-ready files from scans or supplied PDFs, do so without altering the design.

Deliverables  
• Gently enhanced, replication-ready 16-bit / 44.1 kHz WAVs  
• Print-ready CMYK files for disc face, booklet and tray card (matching the original layout)  
• Final glass-master or DDP image plus proofs ready for the plant

I’ll supply the digital album and high-resolution artwork files I have on hand as soon as we start. Let me know your preferred workflow, any specs the plant might need, and an estimated timeline for turning this around.

jobs.title: AI Assistant Content Quality Reviewer
jobs.description:
We’re building AI assistants that help with the everyday parts of life. They write things like suggestions, explanations, reminders, and refusals, and we need someone who can look closely at that writing and tell us where it feels off.

This isn’t just about fixing grammar. The bigger focus is tone and clarity. Does a message sound too cold for someone having a rough week? Does a refusal feel fair and clear, or vague and evasive? Does an explanation actually help the person understand?

You’ll review batches of AI-generated writing, compare them against a rubric, point out what isn’t working, and suggest a better version. You’ll also explain your reasoning in a way that’s easy for anyone to understand.

We’re looking for someone with near-native written English and real experience in editing, teaching, or translation. You don’t need a technical background or any previous AI experience.

The role is fully remote and open to any time zone. Most people work two to four sessions per week and choose their own schedule. Pay is hourly, and you’ll know the rate before committing. There are no regular meetings.

To apply, send us a short note and one example of something you’ve edited. The process includes a paid exercise that takes less than an hour, followed by one conversation. We don’t ask candidates to do unpaid work.

jobs.title: Custom WP Booking Calendar Plugin
jobs.description:
I need a fully-fledged WordPress booking calendar built from scratch for my brand. Once installed, the plugin has to sync seamlessly with Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar and Apple Calendar, keeping availability and confirmations perfectly aligned in both directions.

Core functionality I expect at launch  
• Customers can pick time slots I define in the backend, with the option for me to create one-off or recurring availability patterns.  
• Reminder notifications (email and, if you can, push/ICS alerts) fire automatically at configurable intervals.  
• Recurring bookings are handled elegantly, obeying exceptions or blackout dates I set.  
• Slot lengths, buffers and daily limits stay fully customizable from an intuitive settings panel.  

Interface & UX  
The front-end widget should feel clean and modern, matching contemporary WordPress themes without heavy styling. In the admin area, a streamlined React/Vue-like feel is welcome, but stick to WordPress guidelines so updates remain painless.

Technical notes  
– Please code it as a standard installable .zip plugin (no child-theme hacks).  
– Use WordPress hooks/APIs only; no hard-coded paths.  
– Calendar sync may rely on the official Google, Microsoft and Apple calendars’ APIs/OAuth flows. Store tokens securely.  
– I will need shortcodes and/or a Gutenberg block for easy placement.  
– Hand over documented source, basic user guide and a changelog so I can maintain future versions.

Acceptance criteria  
1. Install, activate, connect calendars, set slots in under 10 minutes.  
2. Create a booking on the site → appears instantly in all three external calendars.  
3. Cancel on an external calendar → removes the booking on the site.  
4. Notifications trigger at the chosen interval.  
5. Core PHP/JS passes WP_DEBUG with no errors or deprecated notices.

If you have past SaaS or plugin examples that show similar calendar sync, that will help me decide quickly.
Cancellations will be handled by instructors individually

jobs.title: Everyday AI Product Tester Needed
jobs.description:
Product Tester, Everyday AI
Remote | Part time | Independent contractor | Any time zone

Role: Product Tester, Everyday AI
Engagement: Independent contractor, part time
Location: Fully remote, any time zone
Commitment: Typically two to four sessions a week, scheduled by you
Reports to: A cohort lead
Pay: Hourly, by level. Stated before you commit.

AfterQuery is building a small family of AI assistants for the ordinary parts of a person’s week. We are looking for people to use them for real and tell us precisely what is wrong with them.

ABOUT THE WORK

Our assistants work on the recurring, unglamorous things: keeping a schedule and the commitments that go with it, planning meals and getting the shopping right, everyday money, errands and journeys, and the administrative post that has to be dealt with. They are narrow on purpose. None of them is a general assistant, and each one is meant to know where its own edges are.

We run a lot of automated evaluation, and it is good at what it does. It catches factual errors, broken output, crashes and regressions. What it cannot catch is an answer that is correct and still wrong: the right suggestion at a moment the person cannot act on it, a decision the assistant made that was the user’s to make, a product that is individually reasonable and collectively exhausting to live with. Those failures need a person who was actually there.

That is what this role is. You use the products the way their owners will, notice where they behave in a way a thoughtful person would not, and turn that into a report precise enough for an engineer to reproduce on a Tuesday morning without you in the room. Both halves are the job.

WHAT YOU WOULD BE DOING

- Running assigned test scenarios end to end and writing up what happened.
- Using an assigned product in your own life for a week at a time, and keeping a short daily log while you do.
- Probing deliberately for the failures that only show up in a life already in progress, rather than on a clean test account.
- Filing defects with reproduction steps, what you expected, why you expected it, and an honest statement of how sure you are.
- Checking that fixes actually hold, including saying when they do not.
- Rating recorded interactions against a fixed rubric, if you take that on. It is scheduled and paid separately.
- Writing a short note at the end of each four week cycle saying what the cycle actually established.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Observation kept separate from conclusion: You can write down what happened in a way that someone who disagrees with your conclusion would still accept as accurate, and then give the conclusion separately. This is the single strongest predictor of someone who does well here, and it is what our selection exercise is built to measure.
Clear ordinary writing: Reports are read by people who were not there. Plain English is enough. Polish is not assessed and long reports are not better ones.
A life the products touch: You keep a calendar, or you cook, or you commute, or you deal with official post. We match assignments to this, because the field weeks depend on it being genuine.
Reliability at low volume: Two sessions a week that actually happen is a better engagement than five that slip.
Willingness to be unimpressed: Including with us. We need people who will say a product is not good enough, and equally people who will say an area is fine so that attention goes where it is needed.

WHAT YOU DO NOT NEED

No software testing background. No QA certification or experience with formal test methodology. No coding, no reading code, and no understanding of how the models work. No technical degree. On some assignments it is better if you have never used a product like these before.

The bar is judgment, not credentials. Our strongest testers have come from teaching, nursing, translation, hospitality management, accountancy and freelance writing. What they had in common was the habit of noticing when something is slightly off, and the discipline to write it down precisely.

TERMS

Engagement: Independent contractor, part time, renewed by four week cycle. No minimum total term.
Location: Fully remote, any time zone. Some assignments include work away from a desk, in a shop or on a journey.
Hours: Typically two to four sessions a week of ninety minutes to two hours, scheduled by you. No standing meetings and no required hours of the day.
Pay: Hourly against recorded time, at one of three levels. The rate that applies to you is stated before you are asked to commit to anything. Onboarding, reading, and the selection exercise are all paid.
Equipment: A current computer and phone. Nothing to buy. Where an assignment needs hardware you do not have, we lend it.
Responsiveness: One working day for ordinary messages. There is one short list of safety matters that need a response within the hour, and nothing else in the role is urgent.

HOW TO APPLY

1. A short form. Where you are, roughly what your week looks like, and which of our domains your actual life touches. A CV is accepted and is not read closely. There is no cover letter.
2. A paid exercise, under an hour, in your own time. You are given a recorded interaction with an assistant and asked to write it up. There is no single correct answer and there are several ways to do well.
3. A conversation of about forty minutes, mostly about your exercise. No panel, no second round, no presentation.

The whole process takes about two weeks. We do not ask for unpaid work at any stage. If the exercise takes you longer than an hour, stop and send what you have; that is a real instruction and not a test.

ONE THING WORTH KNOWING FIRST

The work is quiet, detailed and repetitive in places, and its pleasures are small and specific: the moment you can name what was wrong with something that merely felt wrong, and the moment a product changes because you wrote a paragraph carefully. People who enjoy that tend to stay for many cycles. If you are looking for a route into a different role in AI, this is honestly not one, and we would rather say so now than have you find out in three months.

AfterQuery hires without regard to background, and we assess the exercise before we look at anything else in an application. If you need an adjustment at any point in the process, ask, and it will not form part of the assessment.

jobs.description:
I have an idea for an iPhone app that lets users simply speak a grocery list, parses every item with Whisper-style speech recognition, looks up prices across participating retailers, and highlights the cheapest practical way to buy everything.  

What I need from you is a concise yet technically thorough software-development plan that turns this concept into an executable roadmap.

Core scope  
• Speech input: assume use of Whisper (or an equally accurate on-device/edge model) to turn natural speech into text.  
• List structuring: the plan must cover how we map that raw text into standardised grocery product names and quantities.  
• Price engine: devise a flow for querying multiple retailer catalogues and promotions, then ranking the results on final basket cost.  
• Brand handling: include a mechanism for users to express brand preferences and, by default, have the algorithm favour store brands over national or organic alternatives while still allowing flexibility.  
• iOS-first: lay out the recommended architecture (Swift / SwiftUI, Combine, Core Data or CloudKit, etc.) along with any backend or third-party services you feel are unavoidable.  

Deliverables  
1. A written architecture document (1-2 pages per module) covering data models, service layers, and key classes.  
2. Sequence diagrams or flowcharts that show how speech input becomes a priced shopping basket.  
3. A milestone schedule with rough time estimates and logical dependencies.  
4. Risk list with mitigation strategies, especially around catalogue data quality and speech-to-product accuracy.  
5. Toolchain recommendations (CI/CD, testing frameworks, analytics, crash reporting).  

Acceptance criteria  
• All five deliverables are returned in a single, well-organised PDF or shared document.  
• Each module description includes at least one alternative approach with pros/cons.  
• Brand-preference logic explicitly demonstrates how store brands are prioritised.  
• No section exceeds three concise paragraphs unless absolutely necessary.  

If the outline looks feasible, I will green-light the next phase—detailed UX wireframes followed by development. I look forward to seeing how you’d bring this smart shopping assistant to life.

To secure outside funding, I need a complete startup business plan that convinces lenders and private investors of the concept’s viability. The document should blend a compelling narrative with hard numbers. Please build it around these key components I must present:

• Detailed financial projections: five-year P&L, cash-flow, and balance-sheet forecasts with underlying assumptions (average ticket, table turns, labour cost %, COGS, seasonal traffic, etc.).  
• Investor pitch deck: 10–15 visually engaging slides distilling the concept, market gap, competitive edge, brand positioning, management bio, and funding ask.

I’ll provide raw cost estimates, target lease information, and branding references once we start; please integrate realistic industry benchmarks where data is missing and cite sources. All spreadsheets must be editable (Excel or Google Sheets) and the deck in PowerPoint or Google Slides.

jobs.title: Y2K Non-Compression Activewear Pattern Design -- 2
jobs.description:

The garments must drape comfortably yet still follow the body, so I’m counting on intricate pattern work and smart grading across sizes to deliver that perfect balance of ease and shape. • Digital pattern files (DXF/AAMA and PDF) for all four styles, ready for sampling  
• Construction specs and measurement charts  
• Fabric and trim recommendations with embellishment notes  
• One revision round after I review initial blocks  

Experience with looser fit athletic silhouettes and embellishment-ready designs is a major plus. Share any relevant work, and let’s bring these nostalgic, vibrant pieces to life. Being located in the United States is a HUGE plus.

The finished piece will span roughly four to six half-pages (think folded booklet or slim card rather than full A4 sheets) and should feel light, uncluttered, yet still guide the eye toward high-margin “hero” items.

Here’s what I’m after:  
• Layout that quietly nudges customers toward my most profitable dishes—placement, box highlights, subtle price anchoring, and smart category flow are key.  
• A simple, elegant typographic treatment. I lean toward generous white space, tight iconography, and clear hierarchy instead of heavy graphics.  
• Colour palette is flexible; if a strict black-and-white scheme works, great, but I’m open to a restrained accent colour if it enhances readability.  
• No stock food photos. If an understated line illustration or icon serves a functional purpose (e.g., vegetarian, spicy), use it sparingly; otherwise, let the type do the talking.  

Deliverables

2. Editable source file (Adobe InDesign or Illustrator preferred).  
3. A quick legend explaining the engineering decisions—why items are placed where they are, which receive visual emphasis, and the logic behind any pricing cues.

I’ll supply copy, prices, and category breakdowns once we start. If you’ve previously balanced aesthetics with profit-driven menu strategy, I’d love to see an example.

jobs.title: SophiaLiving
jobs.description:
Meta Ads Media Buyer for UK Home Décor E-commerce Brand

We are Sophia Living, a UK-focused home décor and home textiles e-commerce brand offering distinctive, handcrafted and made-to-order pieces, including made-to-measure curtains, wall tapestries, rugs, cushions and other home accessories.

We are looking for an experienced, performance-driven Meta Ads Media Buyer to manage and optimise our paid advertising with a clear focus on sales, conversions and profitable ROAS.

This is not a brand-awareness-only role. Our priority is turning qualified traffic into customers and building a scalable advertising strategy for the UK market.

What we need:

* Proven experience managing Meta Ads for e-commerce brands, preferably in home décor, interiors, furniture, textiles, lifestyle or similar sectors.
* Strong experience targeting and selling to the UK market.
* Ability to analyse our existing campaigns and identify what is working, what is wasting budget and where the conversion opportunities are.
* Build and optimise campaigns focused on Purchases and profitable ROAS, not simply reach, engagement or clicks.
* Develop effective prospecting, testing and retargeting strategies.
* Test audiences, creatives, messaging, offers and campaign structures systematically.
* Improve the full advertising funnel from ad → landing page → Add to Cart → Checkout → Purchase.
* Monitor and improve key metrics including ROAS, CPA, CTR, CPC, CPM, conversion rate and cost per purchase.
* Experience with Meta Pixel, Conversion API and event tracking, and ability to identify potential tracking or attribution issues.
* Work confidently with Shopify e-commerce stores.
* Provide clear reporting explaining results, insights, problems and the next actions — not simply screenshots of Ads Manager.
* Advise us on what types of creative assets, hooks and offers should be produced based on campaign data.
* Scale winning campaigns carefully while controlling acquisition costs.

About the brand

Sophia Living is positioned around unique, characterful pieces rather than mass-produced home décor. Our products are designed for customers who want their homes to feel individual and personal.

Our main market is the United Kingdom, and our Shopify website and Meta advertising infrastructure are already live. We have existing campaign data that can be analysed rather than starting completely from zero.

What we are looking for in the freelancer

We want someone who is analytical and commercially focused, not someone who simply launches campaigns and waits.

When applying, please include:

1. Examples of e-commerce Meta Ads accounts you have managed.
2. Your experience with the UK market.
3. Typical monthly ad spend you have managed.
4. Examples of ROAS/CPA improvements you have achieved.
5. Your approach to testing and scaling e-commerce campaigns.

jobs.title: Angariação Clientes Imobiliário Luxo
jobs.description:
Procuro apoio especializado para identificar e nutrir potenciais compradores de luxo interessados em adquirir imóveis em Angola — especificamente nas zonas de Kilamba, Benfica, Camama e Zango.

jobs.title: Professional Facebook Video Editing
jobs.description:
I have several raw clips ready to be turned into eye-catching videos whose first home will be Facebook, with repurposed cuts suitable for YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and TikTok. What matters most to me is a professional, polished finish—clean cuts, smooth transitions, on-brand motion graphics, readable subtitles, and music that keeps viewers engaged without overpowering the message.

Here is what the job involves from my side: I supply footage, a basic story outline, brand colors, and any lower-third text. From your side I expect thoughtful sequencing, color correction, audio balancing, creative yet tasteful effects, and delivery of an export-ready MP4 along with any project files (Premiere Pro, Final Cut, or DaVinci Resolve—your choice).

Final videos should:
• Meet Facebook feed specs in 1080p (square or 16:9, depending on the brief)  
• Include a 60-second vertical cut for Reels/TikTok (same grade and subtitles)  
• Retain noticeable quality after Facebook compression  

Turnaround is important to me, so let’s agree on realistic deadlines and stick to them. Please drop a link to your portfolio or a recent project that shows professional, polished work similar to what I’m aiming for. We can discuss scope, revisions, and budget once I see your style aligns with mine.

jobs.title: Branded Sales Pitch Deck
jobs.description:
I have a concise plan for a 12–13-slide sales pitch laid out in Excel (each row already lists the slide title and key bullet points). What I need is the full PowerPoint built in our client’s colour palette and typography, exactly as spelled out in their branding guidelines.  

Please transform the outline into an engaging, on-brand deck: compelling layouts, strong imagery and icons that reinforce the message, and tasteful animations or slide transitions where they genuinely add polish rather than distraction. I will supply the Excel file, the brand guide, and any logo or font files you may need as soon as we start.  

The finished .pptx must be in my inbox by Tuesday morning, ready to send straight to the client—no further edits on my side besides text tweaks if required.  

Deliverables  
• 12–13-slide PowerPoint (.pptx) matching the outline  
• All images, icons, and other assets embedded or provided separately  
• Animations/transitions previewed for smooth playback  

I’ll be available for quick feedback throughout, so you can work confidently and meet the deadline.

jobs.title: PDF to Word Data Entry
jobs.description:
I have a batch of PDF files that hold only text but include several embedded tables. I need each document re-created in Microsoft Word so the wording is copied verbatim and every table is rebuilt using Word’s native table tools—no screenshots or pasted images. Consistency in fonts, headings, and table borders has to mirror the original layout so that the finished files are ready for immediate editing and printing.

Your workflow can involve OCR or manual typing; what matters is zero transcription errors and clean, well-structured Word formatting. I will supply the PDFs in groups, and I expect the matching .docx file returned for each.

Deliverables  
• One Word document per PDF, with all text accurately transferred.  
• All tables reproduced exactly in Word, maintaining row/column order and alignment.  
• Final files spell-checked and free of stray line breaks or formatting artifacts.

Turnaround is flexible, but let me know the volume you can handle per day so we can set a realistic schedule.

jobs.title: Plataforma Automática Recuperação de Leads
jobs.description:
Quero desenvolver uma plataforma web que centralize e recupere leads que chegaram pelos nossos canais Facebook, Instagram, Google e, principalmente, WhatsApp. A ideia é:

• Importar e organizar automaticamente todos os contactos gerados por anúncios ou formulários nesses canais.  
• Identificar quais desses leads já receberam orçamento e, a partir daí, colocar-os numa linha de nutrição.  
• Enviar lembretes de orçamento, mensagens de acompanhamento e novas ofertas ou promoções no momento ideal para aumentar a taxa de conversão.  

O sistema precisa permitir tanto envios totalmente automatizados (gatilhos baseados em tempo ou comportamento) quanto disparos manuais quando o consultor julgar necessário. Quero relatórios simples que mostrem status do lead, histórico de mensagens e métricas de conversão.

Aceito sugestões de stack, mas vejo valor em algo que integre facilmente com a API oficial do WhatsApp e com as APIs sociais de Facebook/Instagram/Google. A entrega inicial deve ser um protótipo funcional: fluxos de importação, painel de leads, editor de mensagens e automação básica.

jobs.title: Excel/CSV Automation for Data Extraction -- 2

jobs.title: AI Customer Support Assistant Prototype
jobs.description:
I want to prove that a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow can cut repetitive tickets out of our queue. The prototype must accept incoming customer emails, interpret the question in natural language, search our internal product documentation, FAQs, and support policies, and then draft a concise, helpful reply that cites the source material it relied on.  

If the model’s confidence dips below an agreed threshold it should automatically pass the thread, along with its reasoning chain and conversation context, to a human agent so nothing gets lost in hand-off.

Core tech I expect to see includes:  
• an embedding store or vector DB for fast retrieval,  
• an LLM orchestrator that injects the retrieved snippets into the prompt, and  
• a lightweight email-style chat interface where I can watch the system work in real time.

I will judge success on response accuracy, average response time, resolution and escalation rates, and a short customer-satisfaction pulse survey you’ll wire in.

Deliver to me:  
• the runnable prototype (code and simple UI),  
• a seeded knowledge base built from the docs I supply,  
• setup instructions so I can reproduce results locally, and  
• a brief evaluation report that benchmarks the metrics above.

I’m happy to clarify edge cases or provide redacted tickets once we begin.

jobs.title: Data Entry & Support Specialist
jobs.description:

• Web research – When I need quick facts or competitor information, you’ll gather it, verify sources, and drop it neatly into the sheet or a short summary document.  
• Customer support – You’ll answer basic customer emails or chat tickets using templates I provide, escalating only when something falls outside the script.

The pace is flexible; there’s no hard deadline, so accuracy and clear communication matter more than speed. Familiarity with Google Workspace, solid written English, and a knack for spotting small errors are essential. Experience with Turkish or other listed skills (translation, Canva, social media) is a plus but not required.

Deliverables will be reviewed weekly for completeness, correct formatting in Google Sheets, and courteous, on-brand responses to customers. If this sounds like your kind of steady, varied work, let’s talk and arrange a quick trial task.

jobs.title: Girls Empowerment Nonprofit Website Development
jobs.description:
$30.00 – 250.00 USD

jobs.title: UGC Social Media Post Creator
jobs.description:

Quality matters more than quantity, so I’ll start you on a small batch to make sure the tone feels natural, candid, and on-brand. If we mesh well, there’s room to expand into regular monthly work, potentially adding TikTok down the line.

When you submit your proposal, show me examples of past work that prove you’ve already driven engagement with similar brands. A concise reel or portfolio link is perfect. If your style aligns, I’ll share the product brief, set creative guidelines, and agree on turnaround times before we kick off.

jobs.title: Indonesian Tech Guest Post Outreach
jobs.description:
I run a technology-focused site and want to strengthen its presence in the Indonesian market through carefully placed guest posts. My priority is brand awareness, so I’m looking for contextual, do-follow links that appear naturally within high-quality Indonesian-language content.

Where I need the links  
• Reputable Indonesian industry blogs, mainstream news websites, and active tech forums relevant to software, gadgets, or IT trends.  
• Domains with solid authority, genuine organic traffic, and an engaged local readership.

What I expect from you  
• Pitch, write, and publish original Indonesian articles (600–1,000 words) that align with each host site’s editorial style.  
• One contextual link to my site per article, using a keyword-rich yet natural anchor.  
• A brief publication report for every placement, showing the live URL, domain metrics, and screenshot.

Acceptance criteria  
• All links must be do-follow and remain live for at least six months.  
• Content must be unique, AI-free, and pass Copyscape.

If you have a strong network of Indonesian tech publishers and can handle outreach, content creation, and reporting end-to-end, let’s discuss timelines and the number of placements you can secure.

jobs.title: Discord Server Setup for Game Boosting

jobs.title: Detailed 3D Electrical Equipment Model
jobs.description:
I need a fully-detailed 3D model of a piece of electrical equipment, drawn in inches, precise enough to generate an accurate manufacturing parts list and material take-off. Every component—internal and external—must be represented, down to connectors, fasteners, brackets, and wiring pathways, so that nothing is missed when the bill of materials is extracted.

Scope  
• Build the model from my sketches, PDFs, and reference photos (supplied after award).  
• Maintain strict dimensional accuracy; all measurements are imperial.  
• Organize each part as a distinct, properly named solid or assembly so I can pull quantities directly into a BOM.  
• Provide native CAD files plus neutral formats (STEP or IGES) alongside a compiled parts list.

Acceptance Criteria  
1. All components visually and dimensionally match the references.  
2. Assembly tree is clean, with no suppressed or unresolved parts.  
3. Exported parts list tallies against the model without discrepancies.  
4. Files open error-free in SolidWorks 2022 and Fusion 360.

Let me know any questions about tolerances, preferred file organization, or additional reference material you might need.

jobs.title: Parametric CAD/drafting portal with an AI assistant
jobs.description:
Reference site: https://www.rayon.design

The goal is to build an AI-driven drafting engine that turns raw data and short prompts into well-structured, publication-ready technical reports automatically. At its core, the system must recognise the user’s inputs, pull from internal style guidelines, and generate coherent sections—introduction, methodology, results, conclusions—without manual intervention.  

Key functions I expect from the first release:  
• Natural-language generation that adheres to engineering and scientific writing standards.  
• Template management so different report layouts can be swapped or updated on the fly.  
• A feedback loop that lets users accept, reject or edit each paragraph and feeds those edits back into the model to improve future drafts.  
• RESTful endpoints so the drafting logic can be embedded into an existing web portal; front-end work is minimal, but clean JSON in/out documentation is essential.  

You are free to leverage large-language-model APIs (e.g. GPT-4, Claude-3) or an open-source LLM fine-tuned with domain data, as long as you clearly state the stack. Python is preferred for orchestration, but I’m open to alternatives if there’s a compelling speed or cost advantage. Please factor in common NLP libraries—spaCy, LangChain, Hugging Face—and modern vector databases for retrieval-augmented generation if necessary.  

Turnaround is urgent; I need a functional MVP ASAP. A short demo video or live link that shows “data in, report out” will serve as acceptance criteria, accompanied by a concise setup guide so I can reproduce results locally or in the cloud.  

Once the MVP is signed off, there’s room for follow-on milestones such as multi-language support, advanced citation management, and integration with our internal data lake, so build with extensibility in mind.

jobs.title: 3D Storyboarding & Character Animation
jobs.description:
I have a short narrative that needs to move from script to screen in 3D. First, I want clear storyboards that map out each beat of the plot. From there, I’ll need original character designs—both believable humans and imaginative fantasy creatures—taken all the way through modeling and simple rigs. Finally, I’m after a set of basic animation passes (walk cycles, key emotional moments, and a few short sequences) so I can review timing and camera language before we commit to full production.

The style should match the darker aesthetics and strong emotional intensity of Berserk, with detailed high-quality designs that align with its mood and complexity.

You are free to work in Blender, Maya, 3ds Max, or any comparable 3-D suite as long as source files stay editable. Sculpting tools such as ZBrush are welcome for detailing, and I’m happy to receive preview renders as playblasts or low-res turntables so review stays light.

Deliverables:
• PDF or image sequence storyboard covering the entire story
• Fully modeled and textured human and fantasy creature characters with clean rigs
• Short animation clips (roughly 30–60 seconds total) demonstrating key actions and acting beats
• All working project files, textures, and exports

I’ll handle final lighting and high-quality renders later; right now I need smart visual planning and solid foundational animation. If this sounds like your wheelhouse, let’s bring these characters to life.

jobs.title: High-Volume Food Motion Short Videos of 2-5 seconds
jobs.description:
I manage a catalogue that is constantly growing and now calls for thousands of ultra-short, eye-catching motion pieces every single week. Each item—think sizzling biryani, colourful chutneys, or layered desserts—needs a 3-to-5-second MP4 plus a matching GIF that can live on social, web banners, and in-app carousels.

Core visual treatment  
• Steaming effects that feel natural, rising realistically from the dish.  
• Subtle utensil interaction—spoons scooping, forks twirling, ladles swaying.  
• Slow, seamless rotation of the frame or plate to reveal every angle.  
• Additional props or micro-animations added where the product demands it.

Audio  
Light background music, perfectly looped to those 3-5 seconds and cleared for commercial use.

Current menu focus  
Side dishes and desserts make up the immediate backlog, with more categories likely once the pipeline is solid.

Throughput expectations  
A minimum of several thousand clips per week, so an assembly-line mindset, template mastery, and strong rendering capacity are essential. Automation and batch-processing know-how (After Effects, Premiere scripting, FFmpeg, or similar tools) will be a huge plus.

Deliverables per SKU  
1. 1080×1080 (1:1) MP4, 3–5 s, ≤5 MB  
2. Optimised GIF, same framing, ≤2 MB  
3. Source project file (AE/Premiere) neatly organised and named  
4. Royalty-free music file and usage confirmation

Acceptance criteria  
• Loop is seamless; no visible jumps.  
• Steam, utensil, and rotation timings stay in sync for the full loop.  
• Colours remain true to the reference photo.  
• Final assets meet size limits without artefacts.

Turnaround: 48 h from asset drop, scaled as we grow.

If this workflow matches your capacity, share a short demo run (one side dish, one dessert) that ticks the boxes above so we can lock in the first weekly batch. Quote based on 1000 item of this.

 * Motion Graphics & Visual Enhancements: Custom typography, kinetic text overlays, smooth speed ramping, subtle visual effects, and graphic elements that emphasize key points without cluttering the screen.
Why Work With Me
 * Engagement-First Approach: Every cut, zoom, and sound effect serves a purpose—keeping audiences watching longer and boosting platform algorithm performance.

 * Streamlined Delivery: Fast turnaround times, clean project organization, and high-resolution exports optimized for any platform standard.

BTQ / USDT

User connects wallet

→ places Buy/Sell order
→ orders are matched
→ settlement occurs
→ user receives the purchased asset

BTQ / QUBX

→ views BTQ/QUBX order book
→ places Buy/Sell order
→ orders are matched
→ settlement occurs
→ user receives BTQ or QUBX

Non-Custodial Requirement

Phase 1 — Technical Feasibility

1. BTQ blockchain compatibility assessment

8. Estimated development timeline
9. Estimated development cost

Phase 2 — MVP

Develop a working platform supporting:

BTQ/USDT + BTQ/QUBX

with:

Wallet → Order Book → Order → Matching → Settlement → Trade History

The MVP should prioritize security, reliability and simplicity rather than a large number of features.

Preferred Experience

Strong preference for developers with experience in:

* DEX development
* CLOB/order-book exchanges
* P2P DEX
* Atomic swaps / HTLC
* Bitcoin/UTXO-based blockchains
* Ravencoin or Ravencoin-derived chains
* Blockchain RPC
* Wallet integration
* Decentralized settlement

Open-Source Approach

We prefer adapting proven open-source DEX/order-book infrastructure where the license permits, rather than building everything from scratch.

Developer should identify suitable existing projects and explain what modifications would be required for BTQ.

Partnership Opportunity

We are open to:

* Fixed-price development
* Milestone-based development
* Lower upfront cost + revenue share
* Technical partnership

Developers interested in becoming a long-term BitQube technical partner are welcome.

Proposal Requirements

* Open-source frameworks you recommend

jobs.title: Domestic Cleaner's Scheduling & Management App
jobs.description:
# Freelance Cleaning Management Software

I am looking for a developer to build a professional management application for a self-employed/freelance domestic cleaner.

The cleaner may work directly for private clients while also carrying out work for several cleaning companies. The system therefore needs to manage all jobs in one place while clearly identifying which clients, jobs, income and records belong to each company or work source.

Most cleans are recurring, but frequencies vary, including weekly, fortnightly, every 3–4 weeks, monthly and one-off jobs.

The application should work well on desktop and mobile and be simple enough for a sole cleaner to use every day.

## Core Requirements

### Dashboard

Provide a clear overview of:

* Today's cleans
* Upcoming jobs
* Completed jobs
* Hours worked
* Expected earnings
* Outstanding payments
* Jobs by company/work source
* Missed, overdue or rescheduled cleans
* Daily workload/capacity

### Companies / Work Sources

The cleaner must be able to manage multiple work sources such as:

* Cleaning Company A
* Cleaning Company B
* Agency work
* Private clients

Each company/work source should store contact details, payment arrangements, standard rate if applicable, notes and active/inactive status.

The system should allow filtering and reporting by work source.

### Client / Household Records

Each household should support:

* Client name
* Address
* Phone/email
* Associated company/work source
* Normal cleaning duration
* Hourly rate or fixed price
* Preferred day/time
* Parking information
* Access instructions
* Pet information
* Cleaning product/equipment preferences
* General household notes
* Active/inactive status

Clients should be searchable and filterable.

### Recurring Scheduling

Recurring scheduling is a key requirement.

The system should support:

* Weekly
* Fortnightly
* Every 3 weeks
* Every 4 weeks
* Monthly
* Custom intervals
* One-off cleans

A recurring cleaning agreement must be stored separately from each actual visit.

Example:

**Mrs Smith – Fortnightly – Tuesday 10:30 – 2 hours**

The system should automatically calculate future visits.

### Calendar / Schedule

Include daily, weekly and monthly schedule views.

Jobs should show:

* Client
* Address
* Company/work source
* Time
* Expected duration
* Status
* Notes/instructions

It should be possible to filter the schedule by company and status.

### Today's Work Screen

Provide a mobile-friendly screen designed for use while working.

Example:

* 09:00 – Mrs Jones
* 11:30 – Mr Davies
* 14:00 – Mrs Williams

Each job should support actions such as:

* Start clean
* Finish clean
* Complete
* Cancel
* Reschedule
* Add notes
* View household instructions
* View checklist

### Time Tracking

The cleaner should be able to start and stop a timer.

Record:

* Scheduled duration
* Actual duration
* Start time
* Finish time

Reports should be able to compare expected and actual cleaning time.

### Cleaning Checklists

Each client should be able to have an individual checklist, for example:

* Bathroom
* Kitchen
* Vacuum bedrooms
* Mop floors
* Dust living room
* Change bedding
* Empty bins

Reusable checklist templates should also be supported.

### Visit History

Each actual visit must create a permanent historical record.

Possible statuses:

* Scheduled
* Completed
* Cancelled by client
* Cancelled by cleaner
* Missed
* Rescheduled

Historical visits must not be changed when the client's future recurring schedule is edited.

### Rescheduling

The application must distinguish between:

* **Move this visit only**
* **Change the recurring schedule**

For example, moving one Tuesday clean to Wednesday must not automatically move all future visits.

This behaviour is particularly important.

### Client Transfers Between Companies

A client may move from one company to another or become a private client.

The system should allow this while preserving the correct company/work-source information against historical visits, invoices and payments.

### Travel and Mileage

Support:

* Estimated travel time between jobs
* Business mileage
* Mileage linked to jobs
* Daily/monthly mileage totals
* Configurable mileage rate

Manual mileage entry is acceptable. Live Google Maps integration is not essential for version one.

### Workload Planning

The system should calculate expected workload.

Example:

**Monday**

* 4 clients
* 6.5 cleaning hours
* 1 hour travel

The software should warn when the planned workload exceeds a configurable daily capacity.

### Holidays / Unavailable Dates

The cleaner should be able to block dates or periods when unavailable.

The application should identify recurring cleans affected by these dates so they can be rescheduled.

### Payments

Support different payment arrangements, including:

* Paid directly by client
* Paid by cleaning company
* Hourly rate
* Fixed price
* Cash
* Bank transfer
* Other methods

Track:

* Amount expected
* Amount received
* Outstanding amount
* Payment date
* Payment method
* Who is responsible for payment
* Paid/partial/unpaid status

### Invoicing

Include basic invoicing with:

* Invoice number
* Client/company
* Date
* Work completed
* Amount
* Due date
* Payment status
* Printable invoice view

Automatic invoice creation following completion of a clean would be desirable.

### Expenses

Allow recording of business expenses such as:

* Cleaning products
* Equipment
* Parking
* Fuel
* Vehicle costs
* Insurance
* Telephone
* Software
* Advertising
* Other expenses

### Reports

Reports should include:

* Monthly income
* Income by company
* Private-client income
* Hours worked
* Jobs completed
* Average clean duration
* Average job value
* Expenses
* Mileage
* Outstanding payments
* Estimated profit
* Workload by day/week/month

CSV export would be useful.

### Search and Filtering

Allow searching/filtering by:

* Client
* Address
* Company
* Date
* Job status
* Payment status
* Cleaning frequency

### Backup / Restore

The user should be able to:

* Export a complete backup
* Restore a backup
* Export useful records to CSV

## User Interface

The design is important.

I do not want a basic spreadsheet-style interface or generic admin template.

The application should have:

* Modern professional design
* Responsive desktop layout
* Good tablet/mobile support
* Clear navigation
* Clean typography
* Easy-to-read cards and status indicators
* Simple forms
* Good visual hierarchy

The software is primarily for a sole operator, so usability is more important than complex multi-user administration.

## Technical Requirements

I am open to the technology used, provided the result is reliable and maintainable.

A lightweight web application/PWA would be suitable.

Ideally the application should:

* Work on Windows and macOS
* Work well on smartphones
* Be installable as a PWA where practical
* Work without complicated server installation
* Retain data between sessions
* Support backup/restore
* Use clean, maintainable code

A cloud backend and login system are not essential for the first version. Local/offline storage is acceptable.

## Demo Data

The project should include realistic fictional demonstration data so all main workflows can be tested immediately.

No real personal data should be included.

## Deliverables

Required deliverables:

* Complete working application
* Full source code
* All project/configuration files
* Installation/startup instructions
* README/documentation
* Demo data
* Backup/export functionality
* Responsive desktop and mobile layouts

All source code must be supplied at completion.

## Completion Criteria

The project will be considered complete when:

* Multiple companies/work sources can be managed
* Clients can be created and edited
* Recurring cleans generate correctly
* Individual visits can be moved without altering future recurrence
* Permanent schedules can also be changed
* Jobs can be started/completed
* Cleaning time can be recorded
* Checklists work correctly
* Historical visits remain intact
* Payments/invoices can be recorded
* Expenses and mileage can be entered
* Clients can move between companies without corrupting historical records
* Reports show meaningful totals
* Backup and restore work correctly
* The interface works on desktop and mobile
* No major runtime errors remain
* Full source code and documentation are supplied

## Preferred Developer Skills

Experience with:

* JavaScript/web applications
* Responsive UI development
* Data modelling
* Recurring scheduling/calendar logic
* Local databases/browser storage
* PWA development
* Business-management systems
* Reporting and financial calculations

Experience with CRM, field-service, appointment or workforce-management software would be useful.

When bidding, please include examples of similar work and briefly explain how you would structure the recurring-job system so that changing one visit does not unintentionally change the client's permanent schedule.

jobs.title: Bespoke Websites for New Venture Firms
jobs.description:
The job

We're a small web studio hiring a designer-developer to design and build two websites for a client launching two new venture capital firms. Both need to feel premium and alive: strong animation, strong graphic design, and a polished build from first mockup to deployed site. For now, both sites are brochure-style: a polished, informational presence for each firm rather than a web app, with no logins, portals, or complex functionality. The craft is in the design, the motion, and how the content is presented.

We handle payment and set up the relationship; after that, you work directly with the client. He knows what he wants, but it lives in his head, not on paper. A big part of the job is drawing that vision out of him and turning it into reality.

Site 1: landing page for a new venture firm

A focused, high-end landing page. The bar is a couple of well-known venture firm sites: minimal, editorial, confident, with motion that feels intentional. A temporary wordmark exists and the final logo is still coming, so the palette and type system should let the real logo drop in later. Content includes team bios and headshots (likely needing a consistent treatment such as black-and-white and background removal) and a portfolio of standardized company logos grouped by status (current vs. exited). Domain and DNS are already in place.

Site 2: a second firm, from a blank slate

The same client is opening a second firm with no brand identity yet: no logo, no colors, no type. You create the identity, then design and build the site around it. He likes the structure of one reference site in the investment space but wants ours clearly better executed: bespoke and refined, not templated.

What we're looking for
Strong animation and motion design: scroll-driven reveals, smooth transitions, and micro-interactions that make a site feel expensive without getting in the way.
Strong graphic design: typography, layout, color, and brand identity, including building a logo and visual system from nothing.
Taking someone's vision and turning it into reality: the client speaks in references and feelings, not specs, and you translate that into a finished product he recognizes as exactly what he meant.
Extracting details from the client: you'll be on calls and emails with him directly, pulling out preferences, gathering bios, photos, and logos, and getting sign-off at each stage. Clear, proactive communication matters as much as the design work.
Solid front-end skills: responsive, fast, accessible, clean code handed off in a Git repository that can be deployed and updated without you.
